text: Monday, when curried mutton was chosen for supper at the trainer's house
why: ¶37 and ¶218 state the trainer's household ate curried mutton that Monday night.

text: Monday evening, when the stable-lad's dish was set aside
why: ¶20 says the maid carried the lad's supper down at about nine on Monday, so the dish was set aside that evening.

text: Monday evening, when the opium was added to the stable-lad's dish
why: ¶37 reports opium in the leftover supper, and ¶218 reasons that it was added after the dish was set aside on Monday evening.

text: Who chose curried mutton for supper that Monday night?
why: ¶218 raises this as an open question; the wording does not name an answer.

text: How was the opium got into the stable-boy's dish without the maid seeing?
why: ¶218 explicitly asks which person had access to the dish without the maid seeing.

text: How was the opium got into the stable-boy's dish without the maid seeing? — while the dish stood set aside in the kitchen, before the maid took it
id: q.opium_how=while the dish stood set aside in the kitchen, before the maid took it
why: ¶218 says the opium was added after the dish was set aside, so access during that interval is a reasonable possibility to consider.

text: How was the opium got into the stable-boy's dish without the maid seeing? — the maid's attention was drawn away for a moment
id: q.opium_how=the maid's attention was drawn away for a moment
why: The story shows the maid being distracted on the path by the stranger (¶21–25), so a moment of distraction is a possibility the reader has reason to consider.

text: Did Mrs. Straker know what her husband was about that night?
why: ¶218 names Straker and his wife as the only two who could have chosen the curry, so the question is raised by the story.

text: Did Mrs. Straker know what her husband was about that night? — she knew nothing of it
why: A plain possibility about Mrs. Straker's knowledge, which the story's focus on her as a suspect gives reason to consider.

text: Did Mrs. Straker know what her husband was about that night? — she was in it with him
id: q.mrs_knew=she was in it with him
why: A plain possibility about Mrs. Straker's complicity; her distress and her denial of the dress (¶86–92) give reason to consider it, without the story having decided it.
